t:
That the Acts of Congress listed below are hereby repealed:

    (a) 
The Act of August. 31, 1916, entitled “An Act to fix standards for Climax baskets for grapes and other fruits and vegetables, and to fix standards for baskets and other containers for small fruits, berries, and vegetables, and for other purposes” (39 Stat 673, as amended; 15 U.S.C. 251–256);
 
    (b) 
The Act of May 21, 1928, entitled “An Act to fix standards for hampers, round stave baskets, and splint baskets for fruits and vegetables, and for other purposes” (45 Stat. 685, as amended; 15 U.S.C. 257–2571).

fable.w: This section only repeals two earlier statutes that set standards for fruit and vegetable baskets and containers. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. A tempting reading is that the word "standards" implies rulemaking, but it appears only in the titles of the repealed Acts, and no outside party is brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: That the Acts of Congress listed below are hereby repealed:

opus.w: The section simply repeals two earlier Acts that set standards for fruit and vegetable baskets. Mentioning 'standards' might suggest rulemaking, but the section repeals those standards rather than authorizing any regulation. It sets up no process involving states, experts, companies or the public, so there is no participation under the definition.
opus.s: That the Acts of Congress listed below are hereby repealed:
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The repealed Acts "fix standards" for baskets and containers, and standard-setting can sound like rulemaking. That fails because this section only repeals those Acts. It creates no rulemaking authority, comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply repeals two existing Acts of Congress. It does not establish any advisory committees, public comment periods, hearings, or consultation requirements with outside parties. The repeal itself is a legislative action, and the text contains no procedural mandates for public participation in any subsequent federal decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: That the Acts of Congress listed below are hereby repealed:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that repealing laws that established standards could involve public comment or consultation during the legislative process, but the text itself only describes the repeal. The definition requires the section itself to mandate or describe a participation mechanism (like a hearing, comment period, or advisory board). This section is purely a legislative repeal of prior statutes. It does not create any new process for outside parties to participate in a federal decision.
